sources.title: Analysis and Performance Evaluation of Li-Ion Batteries Using NASA Battery Data Set

evidence.text_snippet:
Charging Method: Constant Current (CC) at 1.5A until 4.2V followed by Constant Voltage (CV) until the current drops to 20mA.
Discharge Method: Constant Current (CC) at 4A until the specified stopping voltage is reached.
Impedance Measurement: Frequency sweep from 0.1Hz to 5kHz.

qualitative_findings: The voltage profile shows a sharp increase during the initial charging phase and stabilizes during the CV phase. Gradual decrease in voltage during discharge with significant drops towards the end.

evidence.text_snippet:
1) Batteries 25-28
• Temperature: Ambient 24°C
• Discharge Stopping Voltage: 2.2V, 2.5V, and 2.7V

qualitative_findings: Batteries operated at elevated temperatures showed faster degradation

evidence.text_snippet:
2) Batteries 29-32
• Temperature: Elevated ambient temperature (43°C)
• Discharge Stopping Voltage: 2.2V, 2.5V, and 2.7V

qualitative_findings: Batteries operated at elevated temperatures showed faster degradation

evidence.text_snippet:
A. Battery B0005
1) Voltage vs. Time
The voltage profile during charging shows a sharp increase initially and stabilizes during the CV phase. During discharge, the voltage decreases gradually and shows notable drops towards the end of the discharge phase.

extraction_notes: This paper is an analysis of the publicly available NASA Prognostics Center of Excellence (PCoE) battery dataset. No new experimental battery cells were fabricated or tested by the authors. No quantitative performance values (such as specific capacity or capacity retention) were numerically reported in the text, so the performance_points array is empty.
